\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter08.GeneralizedNoiseExtensions}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Uniform extended noise mass]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p236-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p260-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p260-b004
}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass}
\leanok
For a finite set $\Omega$, a real parameter $\rho$, and points $x,y\in\Omega$, define
their noise mass to be $\bigl(1+(|\Omega|-1)\rho\bigr)/|\Omega|$ when $y=x$, and
$(1-\rho)/|\Omega|$ when $y\ne x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity after subtracting one from a cardinality]
\lean{FABL.card_sub_one_cast_pos}
\label{FABL.card_sub_one_cast_pos}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
If a finite set $\Omega$ has at least two elements, then the real number obtained by
subtracting $1$ from $|\Omega|$ is strictly positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the real cardinality]
\lean{FABL.card_cast_pos}
\label{FABL.card_cast_pos}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with at least two elements. Its cardinality, regarded as a
real number, is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Real cardinality after subtracting one]
\lean{FABL.card_cast_eq_sub_one_add_one}
\label{FABL.card_cast_eq_sub_one_add_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with at least two elements. Its cardinality, regarded as a
real number, equals one plus the real-valued cardinality obtained by subtracting one
from its natural-number cardinality.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of extended noise mass]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_nonneg}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.card_cast_pos, FABL.card_sub_one_cast_pos, FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with $2\leq m:=|\Omega|$, and let $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$
satisfy $-1/(m-1)\leq\rho\leq1$. For all $x,y\in\Omega$, the extended noise mass at
$(x,y)$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF_apply_toReal}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with at least two elements, let $\rho\in\mathbb
R$, and fix $x\in\Omega$. The extended noise masses from $x$ sum to one over all
$y\in\Omega$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Nonnegative noise mass]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMassNNReal}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b003}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMassNNReal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass, FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_nonneg}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with at least two elements, and let $\rho$ satisfy
$-1/(|\Omega|-1)\le \rho\le 1$. For $x,y\in\Omega$, define the nonnegative noise mass to
equal $\bigl(1+(|\Omega|-1)\rho\bigr)/|\Omega|$ if $y=x$, and $(1-\rho)/|\Omega|$
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate noise distribution]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p236-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p260-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p260-b004
}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.sum_uniformExtendedNoiseMass, FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass, FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMassNNReal}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with at least two elements, and let $\rho$ satisfy
$-1/(|\Omega|-1)\le\rho\le1$. For each $x\in\Omega$, define a probability distribution
on $\Omega$ that assigns mass $\bigl(1+(|\Omega|-1)\rho\bigr)/|\Omega|$ to $x$ and mass
$(1-\rho)/|\Omega|$ to each other element.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p236-b007}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with at least two elements, and let
$-1/(|\Omega|-1)\le \rho \le 1$. For any $x,y\in\Omega$, the probability assigned to $y$
by the coordinate noise distribution based at $x$ is $(1+(|\Omega|-1)\rho)/|\Omega|$ if
$y=x$, and $(1-\rho)/|\Omega|$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Extended noise mass on the diagonal]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_self}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_self}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.card_cast_eq_sub_one_add_one, FABL.card_cast_pos, FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with $2\leq |\Omega|$, let $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$, and take
$x\in\Omega$. The extended noise mass at $(x,x)$ equals $\rho+(1-\rho)/|\Omega|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Extended noise mass off the diagonal]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_of_ne}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_of_ne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $x,y\in\Omega$ with $y\ne
x$. The extended noise mass at $(x,y)$ is $(1-\rho)/|\Omega|$.
\end{theorem}

Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with $|\Omega|\ge 2$, and let $x,y\in\Omega$. At
$\rho=-1/(|\Omega|-1)$, the uniform extended noise mass from $x$ to $y$ is $0$ if $y=x$
and $1/(|\Omega|-1)$ if $y\ne x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlated pair distribution]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedCorrelatedPairPMF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p260-b002
}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedCorrelatedPairPMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF, FABL.uniformPMF}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with at least two elements, and let $\rho$ satisfy
$-1/(|\Omega|-1)\le\rho\le1$. Define a probability distribution on $\Omega\times\Omega$
by choosing the first coordinate uniformly from $\Omega$, then choosing the second
according to the coordinate noise distribution with parameter $\rho$ centered at the
first coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Affine formula for extended noise mass]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_eq_affine}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_eq_affine}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass, FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_of_ne, FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_self}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with at least two elements, let $\rho\in\bbr$, and let
$x,y\in\Omega$. The uniform extended noise mass from $x$ to $y$ equals $\rho$ if $y=x$
and $0$ otherwise, plus the uniform mass $(1-\rho)/|\Omega|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation under uniform extended coordinate noise]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF, FABL.uniformExtendedCoordinateNoisePMF_apply_toReal, FABL.uniformExtendedNoiseMass_eq_affine}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with at least two elements, and let
$\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $-1/(|\Omega|-1)\le\rho\le1$. For any $x\in\Omega$ and any
function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, the expectation of $f$ under the probability
distribution that assigns mass $\frac{1+(|\Omega|-1)\rho}{|\Omega|}$ to $x$ and mass
$\frac{1-\rho}{|\Omega|}$ to each other point is $\rho
f(x)+(1-\rho)\frac{1}{|\Omega|}\sum_{y\in\Omega}f(y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Product noise kernel]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedProductNoiseKernel}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{

Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with at least two elements, let $n$ be a natural
number, and let $\rho$ satisfy $-1/(|\Omega|-1)\le\rho\le1$. For each $x\in\Omega^n$,
define a probability distribution on $\Omega^n$ by independently choosing each output
coordinate according to the coordinate noise distribution with parameter $\rho$ centered
at the corresponding coordinate of $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product noise operator]
\lean{FABL.uniformExtendedProductNoiseOperator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p260-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p261-b002
}
\label{FABL.uniformExtendedProductNoiseOperator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.uniformExtendedProductNoiseKernel}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with at least two elements, let $n$ be a natural
number, and let $\rho$ satisfy $-1/(|\Omega|-1)\le\rho\le1$. For a real-valued function
$f$ on $\Omega^n$, define its image under the product noise operator at $x\in\Omega^n$
to be the expectation of $f$ under the product noise distribution centered at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier expansion of the extended noise operator]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.uniformExtendedProductNoiseOperator_fourier_expansion}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p215-b002
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.uniformExtendedProductNoiseOperator_fourier_expansion}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourier_expansion, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.pmfExpectation_uniformExtendedProductNoiseKernel_productFunction, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexOrder, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_sum, FABL.uniformExtendedProductNoiseKernel, FABL.uniformExtendedProductNoiseOperator, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with at least two elements, let $\iota$ be a finite
nonempty index set, and let $B$ be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ for the uniform probability measure, with one basis vector equal to the
constant-one function. Suppose $-1/(|\Omega|-1)\leq\rho\leq1$. For every natural
number $n$, every real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, and every $x\in\Omega^n$, the
extended product noise operator applied to $f$ at $x$ equals the sum over all multi-indices
$a$ of $\rho$ raised to the order of $a$, multiplied by the Fourier coefficient of $f$
at $a$ and the product basis function indexed by $a$ evaluated at $x$.
\end{theorem}
